author: derekchiang
content: as i understand it (<@543900561460822016> can correct me if im wrong), without a PROOF frame or equivalent, wallets would have to validate leanSPHINCS signatures through VERIFY frames, but VERIFY frames are stateful (STATICCALL) so they cannot be aggregated, whereas PROOF frames execute in a pure context (which is why they are a different frame type) so they can be aggregated.  so if we ship H* without PROOF frame (or equivalent), wallets would need to use leanSPHINCS through VERIFY frames, so when aggregation is shipped they will have to update their code (including the smart account code) to leverage aggregation.  so the value of shipping PROOF frames in H* is to be forward-compatible with aggregation so that wallets can transparently take advantage of the cost savings from aggregation once it ships, as opposed to having to update their wallet/account code again

author: derekchiang
content:
what's less clear to me is whether it's feasible to ship aggregation itself in H*.  my understanding is that:

- to support aggregation at the builder level, the primary blocker is the readiness of leanVM itself.  if we are 100% sure that leanVM is production-ready, the remaining questions would be things like figuring out where to put the recursive proof (https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12549).  so it might be doable to resolve these questions in time for H*?

- to support aggregation at the mempool level, besides the readiness of leanVM and other questions we have to resolve for builder aggregation, we also have a lot of networking/mempool questions to answer, such as the exact aggregation strategy that each mempool node is supposed to take (i've done some sims that showed that the strategy currently in the 8288 spec is far from optimal).  not so sure whether it's feasible to resolve these questions by H*, by like <@427491045308235776> said above, we don't actually have to -- as long as the protocol itself can deal with aggregated proofs, we can ship mempool aggregation outside of fork schedule

so my first question (and i guess that's for <@1481393192950567003> <@427491045308235776> <@750602516613431366>) is -- just how production-ready is leanVM for the purpose of aggregating leanSPHINCS signatures as of today?

author: kevaundray
content:
The current earmark for leanVM readiness including formally verifying the verifiers is July. This should give us enough buffer to account for unknowns, but also not be too late such that it becomes a blocker for shipping H*.


I'd say the indication of production-readiness will be once we've completed the external audits. Given we plan to FV the code to the assembly level, it will be interesting to see if external audits do find anything

author: kevaundray
content: I think right now one of the main blockers for reducing uncertainty with leanVM, is knowing what is adequate performance, which in some sense is a bit dependent on the networking stack and the aggregation topology we potentially go with. It's possible to make leanVM faster at the expense of making it a lot more complicated

author: lightclient
content: i don’t think it is very likely we ship aggregation in H*

author: lightclient
content: the goal we should be trying to achieve is making it so people who start using PQ crypto in H* will get to take advantage of the aggregation in the future without any additional changes to their account

author: lightclient
content: so doing the PROOF frame allows us to turn that on later even if people use it without aggregation initially

author: derekchiang
content:
do you mean elaborating on why you think it's unlikely we ship aggregation in H*?  i'm not very caught up with the progress myself but it sounds like others have been testing aggregation on the Dalsugi testnet so just wondering what you think the main blockers are (not saying i think there are no major blockers; just trying to understand)

again the goal would not be to ship mempool aggregation, but rather just to support aggregation at the block level so that mempool aggregation can be implemented later out of fork schedule

author: lightclient
content: we would need 100% confidence in putting leanVM into the protocol in the next ~3 months if we want to deliver H* roughly on time. that just doesn’t seem likely to me. leanVM is a big project and it will just take time for people to really understand it, the implications, test it, formally verify it, etc. I don’t expect that to happen in 3 months. It also is really not necessary upon the launch of H*, the number of PQ signatures will not immediately account for all signatures on the chain. Even if it did, we can support 4kb sigs for every tc without aggregation with fairly well understood improvements to our p2p. So I don’t see a reason to rush aggregation at all
